projects.name: The years between us
projects.shortDesc: A bachelor's thesis on how war experiences persist across generations — as an interactive app and an analogue card game.
projects.desc:
Between Us, the Years explores how war experiences continue to shape family relationships, attitudes, and silence across generations, even without being consciously remembered.

The thesis combines an interactive digital application, built around scroll and non-linear movement instead of linear reading, with an analogue card game. Its central rule — every drawn card must be passed on, though reacting to it stays voluntary — turns passing-on and silence into something players actually enact.
projects.caption:
The thesis draws on psychoanalytic and social-science approaches to the transgenerational transmission of war experiences, treating memory as social and relational rather than individually stored — passed on through attitudes, affects, and relational patterns rather than concrete content.

The digital application is built from six sections of five chapters each, thirty in total, navigated through scroll and click interaction, conditional logic, and camera movement rather than page-turning — replacing linear reading with a rhythm of movement, pause, and interruption.

Each of the application's thirty chapters is mapped to one of the card game's thirty cards. The game's central rule is that every drawn card must be passed on, while reacting to it is voluntary; points mark where connection occurs rather than rewarding openness or performance, and silence is neither punished nor rewarded.

Development began with research into memory and transgenerational transmission, then continued directly in the digital medium — structure, interaction, and content built in parallel rather than in sequence — while the card game was developed alongside it as an independent, coordinated format.

projects.name: ONDRA
projects.shortDesc: Short description for the project list — one or two sentences.
projects.desc:
ondra is a digital companion piece to the book Energiewende verstehen, developed because climate change and the energy transition are often perceived as too abstract or overwhelming.

Users move through an abstracted world of distinct climatic zones at their own pace. The design follows the logic of a game without its competitive or reward mechanics — interaction serves orientation and understanding, not performance.
projects.caption:
Gamification functions here as a knowledge-mediation strategy rather than a motivational device: complex ecological relationships are made experienceable through action, with a focus on how individual choices are embedded in larger climatic processes. Following current shifts in climate communication from guilt toward individual efficacy, the project surfaces small, realistic possibilities for action rather than moral pressure.

Each climatic zone is built as its own experiential space, conveying knowledge about atmosphere, movement, and interaction through a clear colour and zone concept that supports intuitive navigation.

Research drew on IPCC reports and publications from the German Federal Environment Agency and NASA, condensed into the core relationships and everyday actions suited to playful mediation. A spatial and narrative concept then translated this research into the different climate zones, structured through a storyboard, with visuals, sound, and interaction developed and tested iteratively alongside it.
